title: Complexity from simple rules accounts for most complexity in nature

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Complexity from simple rules accounts for most complexity in nature

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The generation of complex behavior from simple rules and simple initial conditions is ultimately responsible for most of the complexity seen in nature.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I will argue that it is this basic phenomenon that is ultimately responsible for most of the complexity that we see in nature.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 2, “The Crucial Experiment”; section “How Do Simple Programs Behave?” (from p. 23), p. 28. Scope: complex phenomena throughout the natural world

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch02-04: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.22

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Specific natural phenomena can be studied with existing observations, but no dataset or analysis covers the claimed majority of natural complexity. The causal wording also requires discrimination beyond demonstrations that simple programs can look complex.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For selected natural phenomena, compare causal generative models based on simple rules and initial conditions against rival mechanisms using held-out observations. Quantify the fraction of predeclared natural-complexity domains in which the simple-rule mechanism has decisive predictive support.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Most complexity in nature has no defined sampling frame.

Output similarity does not establish causal responsibility.

Natural domains require heterogeneous data and rival models.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.35
analysis feasibility: 0.2
operationalizability: 0.25
data adequacy: 0.1
discriminating power: 0.15

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The phenomenon of complexity from simple rules is computable, but responsibility for most natural complexity is a causal claim about the world. Public morphology covers a biased slice of biological form and does not record the rules that generated it. Existing material can support scattered lookalike comparisons and cannot confirm or refute the universal causal wording.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Inventory complex natural phenomena, determine the actual rules and initial conditions of each, and test whether most of them are simple rules started from simple states. Confirmation requires that causal inventory. Matching a program's output to a photograph tests only a proxy on a few systems.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The generative rules of most natural systems are not known.

There is no agreed catalogue of 'most of the complexity seen in nature.'

Similar-looking complexity is produced by selection and by continuum physics.
